data.title: Nymex Overview: U.S. Crude Prices on Track to End Six-Day Streak of Increases — OPIS
data.description:
Crude-oil and refined product futures prices were falling, but most remained on track to post weekly gains.

The November West Texas Intermediate crude contract was down by 45cts to $97.52/bbl in light trade on Friday. The more-active December contract was down 88cts to $95.62/bbl. The front-month contract is currently nearly $6/bbl above last Friday's settlement.

December Brent crude was down by 18cts to $105.74/bbl while January prices were flat at $103.17/bbl. December prices are $1/bbl ahead for the week.

ULSD futures were on track for a second day of declines, with the November contract falling by 5.6cts to $4.7896/gal, still about 5cts ahead of last week's settlement. The more-active December contract was down by 4.37cts to $4.6108/gal.

Most activity in RBOB was also focused on the next-month contract, with November prices falling by 4.08cts to $3.1394/gal and December prices trading 2.7cts lower to $3.0528/gal. RBOB futures are on track to end the week about 15cts/gal lower than last Friday.

U.S. crude prices have seen a six-day streak of increases as supply concerns have supported the market. Friday's declines come even after the Energy Information Administration on Thursday reported a sharp 8.6 million-bbl drop in U.S. commercial crude inventories.

But those concerns are being mitigated by the announcement by the International Energy Agency that member countries have agreed to accelerate the release of 100 million bbls of crude oil and refined products that they had previously announced would be put into markets.

The release is expected to include about 20 million bbl of diesel.

The week's increase in diesel futures prices is being felt by consumers, with the average retail diesel price Friday of $6.3261/gal marking the fourth day of increases and an increase of about 5cts/gal from last Friday.

Gasoline prices around the country Friday averaged $4.3271/gal, about 6cts/gal lower than a week ago.

Bond Yields Tick Higher After Treasury Doesn't Signal Cuts to Auction Sizes — WSJ
data.description:
By Sam Goldfarb

Longer-term Treasury yields ticked higher after the Treasury department passed on an opportunity to send a strong signal that it is considering reducing the sizes of bond auctions.

In survey ahead of its quarterly refunding announcement on Nov. 4, the agency asked bond dealers for their thoughts on what future changes to auction sizes it should consider "given expected borrowing needs and investor demand." But it didn't say anything more explicit that might have hinted that cuts to longer-term debt auctions were imminent-a signal that some investors had thought was possible given the Trump administration's efforts to push down bond yields.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Crypto.com, Gemini, and a16z among donors in $210.5M flow to Trump super PACs
data.description:
Companies that watched federal enforcement cases against them disappear have since sent serious money to President Trump's political operation. A Public Citizen report published on October 8, 2026 puts the figure at $210.5 million contributed or pledged to pro-Trump super PACs.

Some of crypto's best-known names sit on that donor list. Crypto.com, Gemini, and venture firm Andreessen Horowitz all appear prominently, and the timing of their checks is drawing attention.

The consumer watchdog reviewed the Trump administration's rollback of federal enforcement. It counted 212 enforcement actions that were canceled or weakened, involving 205 corporations.

Public Citizen then cross-referenced those companies against political giving. Collectively, the corporations that benefited have contributed or pledged $210.5 million to groups such as MAGA Inc. and Keep America Great.

Crypto.com stands out. According to the report, the exchange gave $35 million to MAGA Inc. and $2 million to Keep America Great. Those donations followed the SEC's decision to cancel an investigation into the platform over unregistered securities trading.

Gemini's contributions came from both the company and its founders. The exchange donated $20 million to MAGA Inc., while co-founders Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss each personally gave $10 million, bringing the Gemini-linked total to $40 million. Those contributions followed a dropped SEC probe of its own.

Andreessen Horowitz, the venture capital firm often called a16z, also made the list. The firm and co-founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz donated $12 million to MAGA Inc.

The a16z connection runs a little differently. Rather than the firm itself facing a dropped case, Public Citizen found that nine companies in its investment portfolio benefited from the canceled federal actions.

It is worth being precise about what the report documents. It shows a sequence: enforcement was dropped or softened, and donations followed. Public Citizen frames this as a troubling pattern of regulatory relief tied to political giving and raises ethical concerns about corporate money in politics.

The report documents timing and amounts. It does not, based on the findings described, present proof of an explicit exchange of donations for dropped cases.

Gemini's donations came partly from its founders' personal accounts, while Crypto.com's came from the corporate side. a16z's contribution mixed firm and founder money and connects to a wider portfolio of companies.

For investors, the practical question is how much regulatory risk is truly gone versus simply paused. Public Citizen's count of 212 canceled or weakened actions across 205 corporations is a measure of how much changed. It is also a measure of how much could change back.

data.title: Shoppers Stop Swings To Rs 3.11 Cr Profit In Q2 FY27
data.description:
Revenue from operations rose 8.72 per cent to Rs 1,366.27 crore, while the retailer attributed its return to profitability to its premiumisation strategy

Retail chain Shoppers Stop reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 3.11 crore in the September quarter of FY27, reversing a net loss of Rs 20.11 crore in the year-ago period, as its premiumisation strategy supported profitability despite a shift in the festive season towards the December quarter.

Revenue from operations rose 8.72 per cent to Rs 1,366.27 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,256.62 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to the company’s regulatory filing. The Raheja family-promoted retailer attributed its return to profitability to its “premiumisation-led growth strategy”, which it said had enabled a “PAT positive performance”.

Total income, including other income, increased 9.7 per cent to Rs 1,389.15 crore during the quarter. Total expenses rose 7.11 per cent to Rs 1,385.02 crore. Shoppers Stop Managing Director and CEO Kavindra Mishra said the company delivered a strong performance in the second quarter despite the festive season shifting largely to the third quarter this year.

"Our continued focus on premiumisation, experiential retail, inventory discipline and operational excellence is resonating well with customers and strengthening the quality of growth. We remain committed to prudent capital allocation, further improving profitability, and achieving our goal of becoming debt-free by the end of Q3," he said.

Shoppers Stop operates 119 department stores, 12 premium home concept stores, 73 speciality beauty stores featuring brands such as M.A.C, Estee Lauder, Bobbi Brown, Clinique, Jo Malone, NARS, ARMANI beauty and PRADA BEAUTY, alongside its in-house SS Beauty brand. The retailer also runs 82 Intune stores and three airport outlets. Its retail network spans 4.6 million square feet across 75 cities.

data.title: Tata Chemicals Gets Relief As Tribunal Rejects Rs 908 Cr Allied Silica Claim
data.description:
A three-member tribunal unanimously rejected the claim by Allied Silica and promoter Manmohan Singh Jain, but a majority directed Tata Chemicals to pay Rs 1 crore plus interest and certain costs.

Tata Chemicals said on Friday that an arbitration tribunal has unanimously rejected a Rs 908-crore claim filed against it by Allied Silica Limited and its promoter Manmohan Singh Jain, although a majority of the panel directed the company to pay Rs 1 crore, along with interest and certain costs.

The three-member tribunal of the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA) issued its final award on October 15, 2026, the company said in a regulatory filing.

While all three members rejected the claim of Rs 908 crore, a majority of the tribunal directed Tata Chemicals to pay Allied Silica a principal amount of Rs 1 crore, together with interest and certain costs. The dissenting member opposed the payment direction, including the principal amount, interest and costs.

Tata Chemicals said it was examining the final award and would assess its future course of action.

The company had informed stock exchanges on December 11, 2024, that Allied Silica and Jain had initiated arbitration proceedings against it under MCIA rules, seeking Rs 908 crore.

The latest disclosure was made under Regulations 30 and 51 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015.

data.title: FSSAI Issues Notices To Gemini Edibles, BigBasket, Flipkart Over Rice Bran Oil Claims
data.description:
FSSAI flagged cholesterol and heart-health claims made for Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil under the Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018, and raised a separate ecommerce licensing concern involving Gemini Edibles

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued notices to Gemini Edibles & Fats India, BigBasket and Flipkart over allegedly impermissible cholesterol and heart-health claims made in the promotion of Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil. The regulator has also flagged a potential licensing violation by Gemini Edibles over the sale of food products through its own ecommerce website.

In a social media post on Friday, FSSAI said it had issued notices to Hyderabad-based Gemini Edibles and Fats India, Innovative Retail Concepts, which operates BigBasket, and Flipkart India over promotional material for the rice bran oil. The claims included 'Reduces bad cholesterol and maintains/increases good cholesterol' and references to 10,000 PPM Natural Oryzanol.

"The cholesterol and heart-health claims were found to be not covered/permitted under the applicable claims for edible vegetable oil (rice bran oil) under the Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018," FSSAI said.

The regulator has asked the three companies to explain why action should not be initiated against them under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The notices concern the alleged violations, and no final penalties against the companies have been announced in connection with the claims.

Separately, FSSAI said Gemini Edibles and Fats India was found offering or selling food products through its own ecommerce website without appearing to hold a valid central licence covering e-commerce activity.

In other enforcement actions, FSSAI suspended the licence of DNV Food Products Ltd after an inspection found serious non-compliances relating to hygiene, sanitation, storage and licensing. The regulator also cancelled the licence of Jhanvittanni over continued non-compliance with food safety rules and regulations.

data.title: City Therapeutics Shares Leap in Trading Debut After Upsized IPO
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Shares of City Therapeutics rose sharply in their trading debut Friday after the clinical-stage biotechnology's upsized initial public offering raised about $200 million.

City shares were recently changing hands at $22.53, up 25%, after opening at $23.

The Cambridge, Mass., company late Thursday said it was selling more than 11.1 million shares at $18 each in the IPO, compared with prior plans to offer about 9.72 million shares at between $17 and $19 apiece.

data.title: Unique Wealth discloses $10.4 million in Bitcoin exposure in latest 13F-HR filing
data.description:
Unique Wealth, LLC, a registered investment advisor based in Tampa, Florida, reported approximately $10.4 million in Bitcoin holdings in its latest 13F-HR filing with the SEC.

The firm did not buy coins and store them in a vault. It bought Bitcoin through spot ETFs, the route most wealth managers now use to put crypto in client portfolios.

The filing was submitted on October 16, 2026, and covers the third quarter of 2026.

A 13F-HR is a quarterly report. Institutional investment managers use it to tell the SEC what securities they hold.

Unique Wealth's snapshot shows Bitcoin exposure spread across spot Bitcoin ETFs. The largest is the Bitwise Bitcoin ETF (BITB), valued at roughly $5.3 million.

Next is BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), at about $2.1 million. Together, the two funds make up the bulk of the firm's reported Bitcoin position.

The preference for Bitwise over BlackRock stands out. IBIT gets most of the attention in the spot ETF market, but Unique Wealth put more money into BITB.

A spot Bitcoin ETF holds actual Bitcoin and issues shares that trade on a regular stock exchange. An advisor can buy those shares in the same brokerage account that holds index funds and bonds.

The position is real money, but it is small next to the firm's total book.

As of the second quarter of 2026, Unique Wealth's overall portfolio was valued at approximately $858 million. The firm, registered with the SEC under number 801-120294, manages around $966 million in assets under management.

The two figures measure different things. The $858 million is the reported portfolio value from the quarterly filing. The $966 million figure covers the firm's broader assets under management.

The firm's assets have grown steadily, climbing from under $200 million in late 2022 to nearing $1 billion by early 2026. It serves retail and high-net-worth clients.

The approval of spot Bitcoin ETFs in early 2024 facilitated traditional financial advisors in accessing Bitcoin's price movements through regulated channels, without requiring direct custody of the digital currency.

Unique Wealth's disclosure follows a continuing pattern among RIAs. They add exposure through ETF shares rather than large direct purchases of Bitcoin.

The fund choices matter for ETF issuers. Unique Wealth's tilt toward Bitwise shows that brand recognition alone does not decide where advisor money goes.

The other thing to watch is position size over time. Quarterly 13F-HR filings let observers track whether firms like Unique Wealth increase, hold, or cut their Bitcoin ETF stakes.

data.title: Bernstein reiterates Market Perform rating on Venture Global, $14 price target
data.description:
Bernstein reiterated their Market Perform rating on Venture Global's stock with a price target of $14.00.

The price target implies an upside of 12.0% from the Oct 15 close of $12.50.

Key takeaways from the analyst note

Operational Foundation: Venture Global's existing operational framework, including a large private power network for its LNG operations, positions it favorably against competitors who are still in the conceptual development phase. data.title: Uber’s A ‘Compelling Investment Opportunity,’ Says Guggenheim – Flags Valuation Discount Versus Revenue, Profit Growth
data.description:
Key points:
  • Manley argued that few internet companies of Uber’s scale are growing their top line by about 20% and profit by about 40% while trading at a discount to the market, according to The Fly.
  • Guggenheim expects autonomous-vehicle deployments in the fourth quarter of 2027 to more than double from current levels, according to Investing.com’s report.
  • Uber’s autonomous-vehicle division is reportedly undergoing leadership changes, with Sarfraz Maredia set to leave on November 16.

Uber (UBER) shares were in focus on Friday after Guggenheim reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating and $125 price target, calling it a “compelling investment opportunity.”

According to The Fly, analyst Taylor Manley argued that few internet companies of Uber’s scale are growing their top line by about 20% and profit by about 40% while trading at a discount to the broader market.

Manley noted that consensus forecasts for Uber’s 2027 gross bookings are 9% higher than a year ago, even as the shares have meaningfully underperformed the market over the same period.

UBER shares traded 0.4% lower at the time of writing on Friday.

Autonomous-Vehicle Outlook

Guggenheim said Uber’s valuation multiple is largely dictated by the market’s perception of its position in autonomous vehicles, with fourth-quarter 2027 deployments expected to more than double from current levels, according to a report published by Investing.com.

Guggenheim said the three-horse leadership position had widened in 2026, partly because other competitors’ rollouts were slower than anticipated, the report added.

The firm considers Uber relatively better positioned heading into 2027 than in 2026, with gross bookings forecasts implying upside to sell-side consensus.

Robotaxi Expansion Faces Leadership Changes

Recently, Bloomberg reported on October 13 that Sarfraz Maredia, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility and delivery, will leave the company on November 16 to take a top executive role at an undisclosed company outside the transportation industry.

Maredia’s responsibilities will be split between Samarth Kejriwal, who oversees driverless-vehicle operations, and Aaron Emrich, who heads autonomous delivery, Bloomberg reported.

His departure follows other exits from Uber’s autonomous division this year. Guy Peterson, formerly head of business development for autonomous partnerships, joined Also as chief business officer, while former autonomous-unit legal head Lando Juarez left for Bedrock Robotics in June, according to Bloomberg.

How Retail Views UBER

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘Extremely Bearish’ territory amid an ‘extremely high’ participation ratio in the past 24 hours.

UBER shares have dropped over 12% year-to-date.

data.title: Petros Panagiotidis Discloses Control Stake at AI OKTO Corp. with 74.2% Stake
data.description:
Petros Panagiotis Panagiotidis disclosed a 74.2% stake in AI OKTO Corp., held through Pani Corp. The position stems from an Oct. 8, 2026 spin-off from Toro Corp., with the filing dated Oct. 16, 2026. The move places Panagiotidis in control of the company’s common shares, alongside separate super-voting preferred shares held by an affiliate.

Investor Intent

As Chairman and CEO of AI OKTO Corp., Panagiotidis plans to stay closely involved in strategy and operations. He states he may "consider or explore extraordinary corporate transactions" and could "determine to take any available course of action" as circumstances evolve.

He and Pani Corp. may buy more stock or sell shares over time. The group will weigh options while he holds ongoing talks with the board, other shareholders, and management about the company’s direction.

Investor's Background

Pani Corp. is a Liberian holding company controlled by Panagiotidis, who is a Greek citizen. Panagiotidis serves as Chairman and CEO of AI OKTO Corp., Toro Corp., and Robin Energy Ltd., and as Chairman, CEO, and CFO of Castor Maritime, Inc., with majority voting control at Toro and Robin. He focuses on maritime and energy transport businesses and often builds controlling positions to direct long-term strategy.

data.title: Apple iPhone Duo Preorders Are Off to a Strong Start. That's a Win for the Stock. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Angela Palumbo

Preorders for the iPhone Duo have apparently kicked off with a bang.

Customers were able to preorder the iPhone Duo on Friday, although those eager to get their hands on the Duo won't get delivery until the end of January. That time frame, spelled out on Apple's website, signals that demand for the new smartphone is strong.

Apple investors are likely breathing a sigh of relief. The stock was up 1% on Friday to $345.20.

The Duo was announced last month alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Preorders of those phones started on Sept. 12, and they officially became available on Sept. 18. Some analysts have reported that wait times — how long a customer has to wait for a product — for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup have been slowing. That means that customers are getting the new iPhones quicker than some shareholders may like to see, since higher demand tends to lead to longer wait times.

"Considering that Apple raised prices across the lineup this year, raising the risk of demand elasticity, declining wait times against a stable supply backdrop are an increasing concern in our view," UBS analyst David Vogt wrote on Thursday. He rates Apple as Neutral with a $296 price target.

Barron's has reached out to Apple for comment.

Counterpoint Research also reported this week that consumers are holding on to their devices for longer as prices rise amid a constrained memory backdrop. Any disruption to phone sales is a risk for Apple stock as the iPhone makes up a majority of the company's revenue.

There has been hope that demand for the iPhone 18 Pro wasn't booming because consumers were just waiting to purchase the Duo. That would be a positive for Apple, as the iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 compared with the Pro at $1,199. Friday's initial preorder response seems to indicate that may have been the case.

data.title: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Ingeteam Form Strategic Partnership to Advance Power Solutions for AI Data Centers
data.description:
TOKYO, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (MHI) and Ingeteam S.A. (Ingeteam) today announced a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) forming a strategic partnership to distribute, integrate, and jointly develop advanced energy infrastructure solutions for U.S. Data Centers. The alliance combines MHI's expertise in integrated power, cooling and energy management with Ingeteam's rotating electrical machines, power electronics, control and automation, and digital technologies, helping data center operators address power quality and grid-integration challenges created by next-generation AI workloads.

Power Availability and Quality Are Becoming Critical Challenges for AI Data Centers

AI computing is increasing power requirements across data centers and accelerating the deployment of higher-density computing infrastructure. As rack power consumption continues to rise, data center operators are evaluating new approaches to power distribution that can improve efficiency, reliability, and scalability.

At the same time, increasingly dynamic load profiles of AI workloads are creating new vulnerabilities in terms of power quality, where harmonic distortion and voltage imbalance affect operation reliability and equipment lifetimes. Combined with lengthening grid interconnection timelines, this is making grid-coordinated power architectures a growing priority for data center operators.

Combining the Strengths of MHI and Ingeteam

MHI Group brings a systems integration approach to AI data center infrastructure with decades of experience delivering large-scale energy systems, industrial cooling systems and complex infrastructure projects. Supported by an extensive service network across North America through Concentric, MHI integrates best-fit technologies into complete solutions rather than offering as single component.

Ingeteam brings more than five decades of industrial and technological experience, combining engineering and manufacturing capabilities in power conversion systems for power generation, grid integration, control and automation, and energy management. Its technology portfolio encompasses electrical generators, advanced power electronics architectures, battery energy storage solutions, power quality and grid stability technologies, and EMS/SCADA control platforms.

Through this alliance, MHI and Ingeteam intend to collaborate on expanding the availability of Ingeteam's power conversion solutions and related software for the U.S. data center market through MHI Group, while exploring opportunities to integrate selected technologies into advanced energy infrastructure architectures and solutions developed by MHI Group for its customers.

The companies also plan to evaluate areas for future collaboration on next-generation energy infrastructure architectures solutions for data centers, leveraging their respective technologies and expertise. Potential areas of interest include advanced medium-voltage distribution technologies, energy management systems and other emerging solutions for high-density computing environments, subject to further technical and commercial evaluation.

"The challenge is no longer just securing power. It is delivering high-quality, reliable power to support AI workloads," said Shin Gomi, Senior General Manager, Data Center & Energy Management Department at MHI. "Ingeteam's depth in power electronics and power conversion strengthens our ability to deliver complete, reliable solutions for our U.S. data center customers developing AI Data Centers."

"This alliance lets Ingeteam bring our power electronics and grid expertise to U.S. data centers alongside a partner with deep systems-engineering capability. Together, we can provide a bridge between the electric grid and next-generation AI infrastructure, enabling customers to scale computing capacity while maintaining reliability and efficiency," said Adolfo Rebollo, Chief Executive Officer, Ingeteam.

This MOU marks an initial, U.S.-focused step. Both companies will continue working with their technology ecosystems, to bring these solutions to market. MHI is committed to enabling the next generation of AI infrastructure through integrated power, cooling, and energy management solutions. Building on its expertise in industrial systems and mission-critical infrastructure, the company will continue expanding its AI infrastructure portfolio and deepening collaboration with industry partners. Together, these efforts aim to meet the growing requirements of AI factories and high-density computing environments worldwide.

* EMS/SCADA represents Energy Management System / Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems.

About Ingeteam

We are a team of more than 4,000 people across 15 countries, with over 85 years of experience enabling the electrification of the society through innovation. We design, build, and improve the systems that keep clean power reliable, efficient and secure. We apply our technology in the areas of rotating electrical machinery, power electronics, control & automation electronics and digital technologies to the wind, photovoltaic and hydroelectric power, battery energy storage, smart grids, rail traction, aeronautics, electric mobility, shipbuilding, water, iron & steel, mining, green hydrogen and data center sectors. For more information, please visit www.ingeteam.com

About MHI Group

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) Group is one of the world's leading industrial groups, spanning energy, smart infrastructure, industrial machinery, aerospace and defense. MHI Group combines cutting-edge technology with deep experience to deliver innovative, integrated solutions that help to realize a carbon neutral world, improve the quality of life and ensure a safer world. For more information, please visit www.mhi.com or follow our insights and stories on spectra.mhi.com.

data.title: Meta employees said Lula's accounts were hindered during Brazil election, Folha reports
data.description:
Employees at Meta acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were negatively affected by restrictions during the country's election, newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed.

The messages also acknowledged the platform recommended the profile of challenger Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, as well as his WhatsApp channel, according to the report.

  • Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment

  • Lula will face Bolsonaro in a runoff on October 25, following a stronger-than-expected performance by the senator in the first-round vote earlier this month

  • Lula's camp said earlier this week it would file a complaint before the Organization of American States alleging that Meta, which owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook, manipulated social media during Brazil's election

  • According to Lula's party, some of his posts appeared without a share button, suffered reduced reach, and had stories that prevented reactions and sharing, in addition to appearing without audio or playing at accelerated speed

  • A justice at Brazil's top electoral court on Thursday ordered the company not to unjustifiably limit the reach of political content related to both candidates through the end of the runoff campaign

  • The ruling also stipulated that Meta AI, the company's artificial intelligence chatbot, must not favor either candidate when generating election-related content

data.title: Why Fox Can Finally Breathe a Sigh of Relief With Roku Deal-and Why The NFL Can't — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Fox Corp.'s $22 billion acquisition of Roku finally gives the media titan a way to deliver its programming directly to viewers, a huge plus for livestreaming — especially its Sunday NFL games.

The deal, approved by Fox and Roku shareholders this week and expected to close early next year, essentially takes the risk off the table that the NFL will renew its 10-year contract with Fox early. The contract runs through 2033, but has an opt-out clause that either party can exercise after the 2029 season.

An early renewal has weighed on Wall Street — billions spent on tradition TV, the NFL's right to move high-profile games to powerful livestreams like Amazon, and NFL's massive media rights that just keep going up.

And all of these things for Fox without new ways to make money.

Nailing down the deal, though, has analysts singing a different tune because Roku's streaming operating system on TVs will allow Fox to stream live events and gets revenue from ads and subscription fees for other streams such as Netflix and Comcast's Peacock.

On Friday, Bank of America's Jessica Reif Ehrlich double upgraded Fox to Buy from Underperform and raised her price target to $85 from $54. The change drove shares up 1.8% to $65.12 in midday trading.

"One billion reasons to love the Roku deal," Ehrlich wrote, adding that the acquisition "changes the equation" for Fox stock.

Ehrlich said the early renewal risk and Fox's long-term positioning in streaming were behind her Underperform rating.

"With the risk of a near term NFL renewal largely receding until the 2029 opt-out window, the Roku acquisition fundamentally changes the strategic and financial narrative," she said.

Roku provides Fox with a credible path to transition toward a direct-to-consumer model, which has been a weakness for the company, Ehrlich said.

"One of the core bear arguments on Fox has been that the company...lacked a robust direct-to-consumer strategy to fully capture the migration of audiences and advertising budgets away from traditional pay-TV," she said. "Roku addresses this existential question," she added.

On Wall Street, Fox has an average Buy rating with a price target of $77.75, according to FactSet. The stock has six Buy ratings, seven Hold ratings, and one Sell rating.

Fox and Barron's parent News Corp share common ownership.
